newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says port practices need to be transparent.
newsitem.headline: Japan says port practices need to be transparent.

text.p: Transport Minister Makoto Koga said on Friday that Japan's port practices needed to be more transparent.
The U.S. government claims that Japanese port practices discriminate against foreign vessels.

The Federal Maritime Commission (FMC) said on Wednesday that it would slap $100,000 surcharges on Japanese vessels calling at U.S. ports in retaliation for what it termed "unfavourable restrictive practices".

Washington has said that the Japan Harbour Transportation Association (JHTA), which is made up of port cargo-handling firms and mediates between labour unions and shipping companies, has put in place costly and restrictive practices that discriminate against foreign vessels.
The U.S. commission said the JHTA exercises its control through a "prior consultation" system of negotiations and pre-approvals involving carriers, the JHTA and waterfront unions.
"It is a matter of private sector practices. It is difficult for the government to intervene in a matter involving labour unions," Koga said.
He said the JHTA and waterfront unions are saying they will not change the "prior consultation" system.
"We have to respect their intention. But I think we should make the system more transparent as the U.S. and Japan's shipping firms are calling for more transparency," he said.
